hints: Every rotation is a length-n substring of the string doubled.
Compare candidate starting positions without comparing their common prefix again.
Booth's algorithm discards a whole range of starts after the first mismatch.
analogy: Two runners compare rotations; the runner with the larger next character and all starts it has passed can be eliminated.
example: For acab, the rotations are acab, caba, abac, baca; abac is smallest.
algorithm: Run Booth's minimum-rotation algorithm on s+s: keep two distinct candidate starts and an offset. Increase the offset while characters match. At a mismatch, advance the candidate with the larger character past the compared prefix, keep the starts distinct, and reset the offset. Output n characters from the surviving start.
correctness: After a mismatch, every skipped start is beaten by a corresponding rotation beginning in the other compared block; therefore no discarded start can be uniquely optimal. The remaining candidate is minimal.
complexity: For length n, O(n) time and O(n) space for the doubled string.
